evidence: training and classification data are intermixed using 5-fold cross-validation

unresolved: n_models counted as 2 (decision tree, SVM); the paper also separately analyses a linear-kernel SVM vs RBF-kernel SVM in the evasion section (Section 6), which could be read as a third variant rather than a hyperparameter choice of the same SVM model.

n_datasets counted as 6 (D1-D6, the named VirusTotal/Google sub-collections the paper itself enumerates in Section 5.1); the paper also frames all of them as one combined ~660,000-file corpus, so 1 is a defensible alternative reading.
n_seeds is null: the paper uses 5-fold cross-validation (not seeded repetitions/trials) and states no random-seed or repeat-run count.

n_baselines counted as 5 (PJScan, MDScan, ShellOS, MalwareSlayer, commercial antivirus engines as a group); of these only PJScan and the VirusTotal antivirus engines are directly run/compared by the authors -- MDScan, ShellOS and MalwareSlayer are compared only via cited literature numbers in Table 4, not re-run. The 43 individual antivirus engines (Figure 5) could alternatively be counted as separate baselines rather than one group.

control_arm set to 'none': this is a malware-detection paper, not a backdoor/poisoning paper, so the clean-vs-poisoned control-arm concept does not map cleanly; there is no unpoisoned reference arm of the type the schema targets.
